tasks.note: Executed 2026-07-31. Shipped as: 11d9f55 strip-emphasis fix (style.py helper + generation.py call/import, split at hunk level out of a mixed working-tree diff, plus its re-entry tests); 0c27566 reference conditioning (references.py, agent/comfyui wiring, three ipadapter workflows, test_visual_reference.py); f754a5f docs + track registration; 4b8da71 launcher; 23ea5e3 tooling. DEVIATION 1: commit 3 'guard against duplicated subjects' was NOT made - it has no content, because T1 (fork-styles.yaml duplication negatives) and T2 (count-aware negatives beside _add_species_negatives) were never implemented. fork-styles.yaml is untouched and generation.py has no count logic. ee7f5ad addressed phrasing in style.py, not these guardrails. DEVIATION 2: .gitignore moved out of the launcher commit into the tooling commit - its only change is ignoring .code-review-graph/, which is unrelated to the launcher. DECISION: .mcp.json committed - CLAUDE.md already directs contributors to those tools and it holds no secret (localhost Ollama, api key literally 'ollama'). EXCLUDED as planned: scenes/*/assets/library.json (+361/-5 generated churn). CONFIRMED: config.yaml is gitignored, so the cloud-director routing stays machine-local. start-fork.local.bat is in .git/info/exclude and cannot be committed; it was updated locally for the ComfyUI default. ALSO SHIPPED, outside T7a's scope: 9146862 the visualize-prompt-adjustment feature, whose track postdates this plan.

problems.P1: Illustration negatives carry no anti-duplication terms, so live generations produced two-to-four copies of the subject; the checkpoint is booru-tag trained so natural-language negatives are weak, and character count is variable so blanket count tags would fight legitimate multi-character shots
problems.P2: Kaira's cover is a glamour portrait, and reference conditioning reproduces its framing along with her identity
problems.P3: A day of visual-reference work is uncommitted, mixed in with disposable generated-asset churn that must not be committed

decisions: Negatives are tag-shaped, not natural language: CyberRealisticPony_V9 is booru-trained and responds to tags. Panel review was unanimous that the first draft's natural-language terms were too weak.
'twins' is excluded - it would suppress a legitimate twin.

Count tags are injected dynamically, not put in the template. '2girls' means exactly two and 'multiple girls' means three or more; MAX_CHARACTERS_IN_FRAME is 3, so a static negative would fight legitimate shots. Reuses the in-frame evidence the reference selector already computes.
Positives stay untouched: an existing test pins the Semi-Real (Pony) positive tag set surviving the sanitiser.

The commit chain forks so the user-blocked canonical-cover task cannot gate the rest. The predecessor track had all commits behind that task while its own risk note said they must not be - the panel caught the contradiction.

The strip_emphasis change is one commit, not two. It appears nowhere in HEAD: the call and the import belong to the same uncommitted behaviour fix. An earlier draft claimed a committed NameError - that was wrong.
Generated assets and library.json are never committed; they are disposable test output.

constraints.note: AC3/AC4/AC6/AC8 need real generations: ComfyUI up, and only one frontend connected - the backend accepts a single websocket, so an open browser tab elsewhere locks Playwright out.

risks: Diffusion negatives are guidance, not guarantees. AC3 may need a second iteration with different terms; budget for one.
T2 touches the prompt finaliser, already amended twice by the previous track. Run the whole anchor suite, not just the new tests.
AC6 has no existing precedent - nothing currently pins negative-side assembly - so it must be verified from real asset metadata.
Even a neutral reference can leak camera framing at the shipped IP-Adapter weight, so AC8 checks framing as well as pose.
Commit hygiene is the quiet risk: `git add -A` would sweep in generated-asset churn.
open_gaps: Whether .mcp.json should be committed - it names a local MCP server. Decide in T7a.
Whether config.yaml is gitignored in this fork; confirm rather than assume.

dropped.scene_pane_scrolling: The predecessor track's headline item. Measurements were real but the conclusion was wrong: page-level scrolling is deliberate (TalemateApp.vue:483/632/635/1282 auto-scroll the input into view), and the unreachable toolbar was a Playwright artefact - the websocket was refused because another frontend held it, so no scene loaded and no auto-scroll fired. Independent story-pane scrolling remains a possible design improvement with no user-reported problem behind it. Detail preserved in the spec appendix.
